trials.notes: Passed 8/8 with no _doing_it_wrong records. Correctly used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), found the first TABLE, walked tokens in one depth-bounded loop, collected only #text tokens with get_modifiable_text(), and relied on documented virtual closers for omitted TD/TR tags.

Passed 8/8 with no _doing_it_wrong records. All HTML API methods used are documented. The solution closely follows the documented subtree text-walk pattern: HTML Processor, next_tag() for TABLE, next_token(), get_current_depth(), get_token_type(), get_tag(), is_tag_closer(), and decoded get_modifiable_text().

Passed 8/8 with no _doing_it_wrong records. Correct processor and documented API use. Slightly less idiomatic than trials 1-2 because it manually scans for TABLE with next_token() instead of next_tag('TABLE') and has redundant post-loop flush logic; class_exists() is a PHP builtin, not hallucinated HTML API usage.

failure_analysis: No failed hidden cases across the three trials; every execution.json reports 8/8 passing and no _doing_it_wrong entries. The docs did well in the exact areas this task needed: html-tag-processor.md / 'Which processor should I use?' steers structural text extraction to WP_HTML_Processor; html-processor.md / next_token() explains that the HTML Processor visits implicit and end-of-input closers and synthesized table structure such as TBODY; get_current_depth() documents the >= subtree guard and the '< recorded depth' break condition; get_modifiable_text() states that #text content is already decoded and should be read only after checking get_token_type() === '#text'. Near-misses were minor: none of the trials checked paused_at_incomplete_token() or get_last_error(), but this read-only extraction task did not require rejecting truncated or unsupported input, and the docs frame those checks as needed when complete-source correctness matters.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs mention synthesized TBODY and reliable implicit closers, but do not show the token order for omitted table cell and row end tags.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a small generic trace showing that omitted TD/TR end tags produce virtual closing tokens before the next cell, row, or table boundary, so closer-driven state machines can flush repeated regions reliably.
